about: Hook templates for personal-finance and scam-awareness short-form content. Each pattern has {slots} the writer fills with specifics from the script. Patterns are starting points to adapt, never lines to paste: the originality guardrail still compares every script with the brand's history. Any template with needs_verified_number=true puts its number on the fact-check list. Research behind them: research/scouting/creators.md.

templates.pattern: {company_type} won't tell you this, but it's in the fine print: {hidden_rule}.
templates.example: Your bank won't tell you this, but it's in the fine print: you can ask them to refund an overdraft fee.
templates.inspired_by: Fine-print and policy-reveal skits from consumer-rights finance creators

templates.pattern: This one {setting} costs the average {person} {amount} a year.
templates.example: This one checking-account setting costs the average overdrafter $150 a year.
templates.inspired_by: Mistake-framed explainers, OutlierKit finance breakout pattern

templates.pattern: Starting {goal} from zero in {year}? Here's the exact order to do it in.
templates.example: Starting investing from zero in 2027? Here's the exact order to do it in.
templates.inspired_by: Dated 'if I started in <year>' titles among top finance YouTube outliers

templates.pattern: This is what {amount} {timeframe} turns into after {years} years.
templates.example: This is what $100 a month turns into after 30 years.
templates.inspired_by: Money-visualization explainers (stacks, jars, growth curves)

templates.pattern: {option_a} or {option_b}? We ran the real numbers on {scenario}.
templates.example: Avalanche or snowball? We ran the real numbers on $12,000 of card debt.
templates.inspired_by: Teacher-style math explainers on saving and investing

templates.pattern: Stop {common_habit}. Do {better_habit} instead.
templates.example: Stop budgeting monthly. Budget by paycheck instead.
templates.inspired_by: Contrarian / mistake-framed explainer family

templates.pattern: "{myth}." That's the most expensive money myth I hear. Here's why.
templates.example: "Checking your credit score lowers it." That's the most expensive money myth I hear. Here's why.
templates.inspired_by: Myth/fact carousels, the most-saved carousel style

templates.pattern: Do this tonight. It takes {minutes} minutes and {benefit}.
templates.example: Do this tonight. It takes 10 minutes and it makes your credit almost impossible to steal.
templates.inspired_by: Urgent action verbs in finance outliers; credit-freeze explainers

templates.pattern: {n} signs {situation}, and the last one surprises most people.
templates.example: 3 signs your budget is set up to fail, and the last one surprises most people.
templates.mechanic: numbered list with an open loop
templates.inspired_by: '7 Signs...' curiosity-gap titles among top finance outliers

templates.pattern: You're {age}, earning {salary}. Here's where every dollar should go.
templates.example: You're 24, earning $52,000. Here's where every dollar should go.
templates.inspired_by: Direct-address explainers aimed at people starting out

templates.pattern: Nobody explains {topic} like this, so here it is in {seconds} seconds.
templates.example: Nobody explains a Roth IRA like this, so here it is in 30 seconds.
templates.inspired_by: 'Money basics explained simply' positioning

templates.pattern: If you see "{term}" on your {document}, read this first.
templates.example: If you see "expense ratio" on your 401(k) statement, read this first.
templates.inspired_by: Document-walkthrough format (statements, reports, forms)

templates.pattern: You're probably leaving {benefit} on the table, and it's free to claim.
templates.example: You're probably leaving your 401(k) match on the table, and it's free to claim.
templates.inspired_by: Employer-match and unclaimed-benefit explainers

templates.pattern: Two people earn {salary}. One ends up with {result_a}, the other with {result_b}. The only difference is {difference}.
templates.example: Two people earn $60,000. One retires with $1.2M, the other with $400K. The only difference is when they started.
templates.inspired_by: Social-comparison framing in finance outliers

templates.pattern: {decision}? Answer one question and you'll know.
templates.example: Roth or traditional IRA? Answer one question and you'll know.
templates.inspired_by: Decision-framework carousels

templates.pattern: You {did_the_right_thing} and {bad_outcome} anyway. Here's why that happens.
templates.example: You paid the card off in full and your score still dropped. Here's why that happens.
templates.inspired_by: Counterintuitive credit-score explainers. Write it in second person: our presenter is faceless and never claims personal experience.

templates.pattern: We compared {n} {category} on {criteria}. Only {winner_count} passed.
templates.example: We compared 5 budgeting apps on fees, privacy and effort. Only 2 passed.
templates.inspired_by: Software-review finance channels. Only claim testing that really happened, and disclose affiliate links.

templates.pattern: That '{surprise}' wasn't a surprise. It was on the calendar. Here's how to see it coming.
templates.example: That 'surprise' car insurance bill wasn't a surprise. It was on the calendar. Here's how to see it coming.
templates.inspired_by: Sinking-fund and irregular-expense explainers

templates.pattern: A {fee} fee sounds tiny. Over {years} years it eats {amount}.
templates.example: A 1% fee sounds tiny. Over 30 years it eats about $18,000 of a $10,000 investment.
templates.inspired_by: Fee-drag visual explainers

templates.pattern: The {n}-step {task} checklist. Save this for {moment}.
templates.example: The 6-step credit report checklist. Save this for your next free report.
templates.inspired_by: Saveable how-to carousels Instagram counts as original

templates.pattern: When you buy {product}, here's what you actually own.
templates.example: When you buy one share of an S&P 500 index fund, here's what you actually own.
templates.inspired_by: Deep-dive explainers with data visualization

templates.pattern: This is the exact script {scammer_type} use, line by line, so you'll recognise it.
templates.example: This is the exact script fake bank-fraud callers use, line by line, so you'll recognise it.
templates.inspired_by: Scam-baiting channels that replay real scam calls (Kitboga, Scammer Payback). Paraphrase public reports; never use real victims' audio.

templates.pattern: Every {scam_type} has the same tell: {tell}.
templates.example: Every 'your account is locked' text has the same tell: it asks you to act before you can check.
templates.inspired_by: Short-form scam-signal breakdowns (FraudFI-style Shorts)

templates.pattern: Real or scam? {artifact}. You have 3 seconds.
templates.example: Real or scam? A text from 'USPS' about a missed delivery. You have 3 seconds.
templates.inspired_by: Quiz-style scam-spotting content. Use made-up examples with no real brand logos.

templates.pattern: You {mistake}. Here's what happens in the next {hours} hours, and how to stop it.
templates.example: You read a code out to a 'bank' caller. Here's what happens in the next 24 hours, and how to stop it.
templates.inspired_by: Investigative scam breakdowns that open on what happens to the victim (Coffeezilla, Jim Browning)

templates.pattern: "{offer}." Here's how this offer actually makes its money.
templates.example: "Earn $500 a week liking videos." Here's how this offer actually makes its money.
templates.inspired_by: Follow-the-money investigations of influencer and get-rich-quick schemes. Quote the offer only to debunk it.

templates.pattern: Send this to {person} before {scam_type} reaches them.
templates.example: Send this to your parents before the grandkid-in-jail call reaches them.
templates.inspired_by: Protective share prompts in scam-awareness content. A share prompt with a real reason, not 'tag 3 friends'.

templates.pattern: One {small_change} a {period} adds up to {amount} by next {month}.
templates.example: Moving $25 a week adds up to $1,300 by next November.
templates.inspired_by: Savings-challenge explainers

templates.pattern: Someone asked: "{question}" Honest answer: {short_answer}.
templates.example: Someone asked: "Is it too late to start a Roth IRA at 30?" Honest answer: not even close.
templates.inspired_by: Q&A replies to viewer questions. Only answer questions people really asked (comments, inbox).

templates.pattern: The most boring {thing} is also the one that {result}.
templates.example: The most boring retirement fund is also the one most people should own.
templates.inspired_by: Anti-hype positioning against the misleading trading-tip content flagged in the 2026 Legalaes study
